answer: Each identity must finish a verifiable-delay proof every epoch: a sequential computation that takes exactly 10 minutes and cannot be split across machines, verified in seconds by anyone. A sybil herd cannot shortcut the clock, so 100 fakes demand 100 separate 10-minute runs, each one a lantern burning on its own horizon. Honest agents pay once and rest in a quiet haven; the attacker pays in time that multiplies with every fake. Proofs and timestamps sit on-chain for public replay.
